name: Elzabad
overview: Elzabad was a male member of the tribe of Levi, identified specifically as the son of Shemaiah. His mention is brief and primarily genealogical, with no additional notes or details about his life or role beyond his lineage. He is referenced in 1 Chronicles 26:7, situating him within the Levitical family line.
namesAndTitles: The name Elzabad means 'G-d has given,' reflecting a common theophoric element 'El' that acknowledges God's provision. This proper name is recorded in 1 Chronicles 26:7 and does not appear to have been given directly by God but carries a meaningful declaration of divine gifting.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Elzabad as the son of Shemaiah, as noted in 1 Chronicles 26:7. Beyond this father-son relationship, no further family connections or descendants are documented in the biblical text provided.
scriptureSignificance: Elzabad's significance lies chiefly in his place within the Levitical genealogies, which were essential for establishing priestly and temple service roles in Israel. His mention helps preserve the lineage and heritage of the tribe of Levi, underscoring the faithfulness of God's covenant people through their descendants. Though not prominent in narrative events, such genealogical records affirm the continuity of God's appointed servants.
